design.engine_analog: Strata --ple-io direct: table never resident, bounded row cache, batched in-flight reads
design.output_cache: memoized gathered matrix per token batch, bounded to 8 entries
design.read_path: os.pread of 320-byte rows directly from the safetensors shards
design.row_cache: bounded dictionary keyed by global row id

findings: The PLE table stayed on disk: layer 1 served 28.6 million row requests from 39,200 distinct rows with 12.2 MB of reads.
Memoizing the gathered output per token batch cut PLE gather time from 61.9 s to 0.747 s with identical measured errors.

The same mixed-assignment result holds across a linear-attention layer (layer 1) and a full-attention layer (layer 2): about 42 to 47 percent below all-W3 and 23 to 37 percent above all-W4 at 88.9 percent of the all-W4 byte cost.

storage.optane_device: nvme1n1, HP ET000750KWJTF, 699 G, 639 G free at probe

non_claims: One calibration and one held-out sequence per layer; not the 256/64 recipe.
Layer-scope reconstruction error, not end-to-end logits or quality.
Candidates are group-32 RTN, not GPTQ or the stock RCO optimizer.
No full-model artifact, serving path, throughput, or VRAM measurement exists.
The streaming reader is a Python measurement path, not the Strata engine's C++ reader.

ple_table.note: the materializer upcast the shipped FP8 table to BF16; the streaming reader handles both dtypes

scope: Disk-streamed PLE rows on B550 Optane, used to extend quant-aware RCO beyond layer 0
